question.knowledge_point: Finding a Moment in Time When a Particle is Stationary
question.problem:
The position $x(t)$ of a particle (in meters) at time $t$ seconds is given by 

$$
x(t)={t}^{2}-10t-2,\,t\ge 0.
$$

Calculate the time at which the particle is stationary.
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to calculate the velocity function. We can do that by taking the derivative of the position function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-10t-2) \\  & =2t-10\end{aligned}
$$

The particle is stationary when $v=0\,\text{m/s}.$ So, we set $v=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2t-10 & =0 \\ 2t & =10 \\ t & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the particle is stationary at $t=5\,\text{s}.$

evidence.solution_quote: Therefore, the particle is stationary at $t=5\,\text{s}.$
